newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Rains strengthen prospects for unchanged EU farm set-aside.
newsitem.headline: Rains strengthen prospects for unchanged EU farm set-aside.

text.p: Recent rain, if it continues, would hit prospects of a record crop and increase the likelihood of an unchanged 1998 cereals set-aside of five percent, a senior European Commission agriculture source said on Monday.
Rain, after a long dry spell in much of Europe, initially raised expectations of an even bigger harvest than the record 202 million tonnes of 1996.
Another record crop would fuel demands to curb production and prevent grain mountains reappearing.
"That's not so likely now," the source said, adding that this year's crop would probably be a little smaller.

With intervention grain stocks at a very low level of less than two million tonnes, Commission sources note there is little safety margin in the event of harvest "hiccups" and this would make it difficult to raise set-aside and curb production.
An industry source expected that although total production could be around 200 million tonnes, "useable" production could be much lower if quality suffered due to wet weather.
The Commission source cautioned that last year the harvest estimate jumped by some 11 million tonnes in a few days following good weather at a crucial point in the crop cycle.
Last week in Luxembourg, EU farm ministers unanimously called for an unchanged five percent set-aside rate next year.
But Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler said he would not be rushed into making a proposal until he had more crop data.
He is expected to recommend a rate in time for a formal decision to be taken at the next farm council on July 22.
